title: The three forest friends
summary: A rabbit, a hedgehog and a squirrel all want the same apple, hanging way up high. Each one tries alone, and each one, in their own way, fails completely.

scenes.text:
Lola the rabbit saw it first.

It was at the very top of the big apple tree, hanging from the last branch: a red apple, round and so shiny it looked pretend.

"Mine," said Lola.

And since she was the fastest in the forest, she didn't think twice. She took a run-up, bent her back legs, and sprang.

She didn't get halfway.

She tried again, higher. And again, with her ears stretched right up in case that helped. The apple was still up there, swaying a little, as if it were laughing at her.

"That apple's mine," said a voice behind her.

It was Pim the hedgehog, coming out of the ferns with a leaf stuck to his spines.

"It isn't yours," said Lola. "I saw it first."

"I saw it yesterday," said Pim. "Yesterday comes before today."

Lola didn't know what to say to that, so she crossed her paws.

Pim was strong, but short and rather round. He grabbed the trunk with all four paws, climbed a little, climbed a little more… and his paws slipped.

He fell on his back, curled into a ball, and rolled all the way down the slope until he bumped into a stone.

Bump.

Lola covered her mouth. She didn't want to laugh. But she laughed a tiny bit.

Then something came racing down the trunk, head first, at top speed.

It was Sara the squirrel, her tail so fluffed up it looked twice as big as she was.

"What's going on?" she asked. "I can hear the shouting from my house."

"That apple's mine," said Lola and Pim at the same time.

Sara looked up.

"I can reach it," she said. "I can climb up there without a hair out of place."

And she did. But when she got to the apple and tried to pull it off, she found it weighed almost as much as she did. She tugged and tugged, and very nearly fell off the branch, apple and all.

She came down slowly, her ears drooping.

The three of them sat under the tree without a word, looking at the apple.

It was Pim who spoke first.

"I'm strong," he said slowly, "but I can't reach."

"I can reach," said Sara, "but I can't carry it."

Lola thought about it. She looked at Pim. She looked at Sara. She looked at the tree.

"And I'm tall when I stretch," she said.

The three of them looked at each other.

Pim planted himself firmly against the trunk. Lola put a big leaf over his back, so as not to get prickled, and climbed on top very carefully. And Sara scrambled up over both of them to the last branch, held on tight, and gave the apple's stalk one good bite.

The apple dropped.

And Lola, who was right underneath, caught it in both paws.

Now it had to be shared.

"The biggest piece for me," said Pim, "because I was the ladder."

"For me," said Sara, "because I'm the one who got it loose."

Lola said nothing. She split the apple with her teeth, very carefully, into three exactly equal pieces.

The three of them sat in a ring and ate it slowly. It was sweet and juicy, and every bite went crunch.

"It's the tastiest apple in the world," said Pim, with his mouth full.

"That'll be because the three of us got it," said Sara.

Lola didn't answer. She was looking up, because on the next branch there was another apple, even redder.

"Tomorrow," she said.

And the other two burst out giggling.
